activeQuestion.prompt: Which version could the museum display now under both of the curator’s rules?
activeQuestion.promptZh: 按照策展人的兩項規則，博物館現在可以採用哪一種展示方式？

options.text: Show “BOAT PINS” and state as a museum finding that the tin held biscuits, citing the recording.
options.zh: 呈現「BOAT PINS」原文，並引用錄音，將「鐵盒曾裝餅乾」寫成博物館的研究結論。
options.whyZh: 保留原文字樣符合第一項，但錄音只提到分享食物，沒辨認這個鐵盒，也沒證實盒裡是餅乾。

options.text: Show “BISCUITS” instead of “BOAT PINS” and identify the biscuit story as Ada’s recollection.
options.zh: 以「BISCUITS」取代「BOAT PINS」，並把餅乾故事註明為艾達的回憶。
options.whyZh: 標明回憶來源符合第二項，但拿掉文物原文違反第一項。

options.text: Show “BOAT PINS” and report that the two former workers both identified the tin as a food container.
options.zh: 呈現「BOAT PINS」原文，並寫兩名昔日員工均確認這個鐵盒是裝食物的容器。
options.whyZh: 另一名員工的錄音沒有辨認容器，不能把談話改寫為兩人都確認同一個鐵盒。

options.text: Show “BOAT PINS” and explain that Ada recalled the tin being used for biscuits.
options.zh: 呈現「BOAT PINS」原文，並說明艾達回憶這個鐵盒曾用來裝餅乾。
options.whyZh: 照錄原文，並把用途清楚歸於親歷者的回憶，而不是把它寫成已獲獨立來源佐證的結論。

activeQuestion.explanationZh: 錄音沒有指認同一個鐵盒，無法佐證館方結論。策展人仍可保留文物上的原文，並註明餅乾是艾達的回憶；兩項規則都能遵守。
activeQuestion.evidence: Paragraphs 1 and 2: recording did not identify the tin; original-object wording stays; a museum finding needs independent corroboration about the same object and claim.

group.title: What the Tin Was Called
group.passage:
From a fictional neighborhood museum’s exhibition blog

When the Hollybank Neighborhood Museum found a tin labeled “BOAT PINS” among items donated from the old ferry office, the first draft of its exhibition label described it as a container for spare parts. Former ferry clerk Ada Moore laughed when she read the draft. “We wrote ‘boat pins’ because anything marked ‘biscuits’ would have been gone before the evening crew arrived,” she said. The museum had an undated recording in which another worker mentioned sharing food on evening shifts, but the worker never identified the container.

Before opening, the curator set two rules. The exact wording on a donated object would appear as part of its display, even if visitors might mistake it for a literal description. And a firsthand recollection could appear beside an object, but it could be presented as the museum’s own finding only if a second independent source identified that same object and supported the specific claim being made.

At a preview, a teacher suggested replacing “BOAT PINS” on the display with “BISCUITS” so children would understand the story. The curator replied, “We can make the label clearer without giving it the last word.” She pointed to a space reserved for visitor notes: one family had already offered to bring in a photograph of the ferry staff break room.
group.passageZh:
以下是虛構的社區博物館展覽部落格文章。

霍利班克社區博物館在舊渡輪辦公室捐出的物品中找到一個寫著「BOAT PINS」（船用銷釘）的鐵盒。展覽說明牌的初稿將它描述為存放備用零件的容器。曾任渡輪站務員的艾達・摩爾讀了初稿，忍不住笑了。她說：「我們在盒上寫『船用銷釘』，因為只要寫上『餅乾』，還沒等晚班同事來上班，裡頭的東西就會被吃光。」博物館有一段未註明日期的錄音，另一名員工在錄音中提到大家會在晚班時分享食物，但未指認那個容器。

展覽開幕前，策展人訂了兩項規則。捐贈文物上的原文要在展出時呈現，即使參觀者可能按字面誤解也一樣。親歷者的回憶可以放在文物旁，但只有在第二個獨立來源能辨認出同一件文物，且能支持該項說法時，博物館才能把這項說法列為館方的研究結論。

在預展上，有位老師建議把展示中的「BOAT PINS」換成「BISCUITS」（餅乾），讓孩子更容易了解這段故事。策展人回答：「我們可以把說明寫清楚，但不必把它當作最後定論。」她指向留給訪客補充資料的地方：已經有一家人表示願意帶來一張渡輪員工休息室的照片。

originalQuestion.prompt: How must an authorized urgent movement be communicated?
originalQuestion.promptZh: 核准的緊急物料異動應如何傳達？

options.text: Only through a quick verbal message
options.whyZh: 通知明說不能只靠口頭通知。

options.text: By changing the stock list without a record
options.whyZh: 與需要臨時異動紀錄的要求矛盾。

options.text: By omitting it until next quarter
options.zh: 先不記錄，等到下一季再處理
options.whyZh: 當期盤點須掌握異動，不能省略。

options.text: On a temporary movement sheet copied to the counting team
options.zh: 記在臨時異動表並交副本給盤點團隊
options.whyZh: 通知明確要求書面紀錄及副本。

originalQuestion.explanationZh: 通知明確要求書面紀錄及副本。
